CONFIDENTIAL - HR INVESTIGATION FILE
AWATERE DISTRICT COUNCIL
Witness Statement in the matter of Ferguson v Kellogg
I, Angela Michelle Torres of 27 Kowhai Street, Awatere 4310, a Senior Planner employed by
Awatere District Council, make this statement knowing that it will be used for the purposes of an
internal HR investigation under the Council's Positive Workplace Policy. The matters recorded are
true to the best of my knowledge and belief.
Background
I have been employed by Awatere District Council since August 2016. I report directly to Priya
Sharma and work in a team that includes Helen Ferguson (my immediate team leader) and David
Kellogg (a peer in terms of grade but a senior technical lead). I have known Mr Kellogg
professionally for approximately seven years and Ms Ferguson for about four.
Incident - 17 November 2025 team meeting
During our weekly team meeting Mr Kellogg interrupted Ms Ferguson while she was presenting the
consents pipeline update. His words, as best I can recall, were: "Honestly Helen, if you actually
understood s104 you'd know this is nonsense." Ms Ferguson did not respond in the meeting. After
the meeting I spoke with Ms Ferguson in the tearoom and she was visibly upset. I recorded a brief
file note on my work phone the same afternoon (screenshot available on request).
Incident - 11 February 2026
I was present in the open-plan area outside Ms Ferguson's office on the morning of 11 February
2026. Junior planner Jonathan Briggs was also there, seated at his desk opposite mine. Mr Kellogg
approached Ms Ferguson at her office door. His voice was raised sufficient that I could clearly
overhear. The relevant part of what he said, as I recall it, was: "you're out of your depth Helen -
let's be honest, you got this job because they needed a woman on the panel." I noted at the time
that Ms Ferguson went pale and did not respond. Mr Briggs made eye contact with me. I recorded

the statement in an email to myself from my work account at 11:17am that day (attached as
Appendix A).
Broader context (offered voluntarily)
I wish to add that Mr Kellogg's conduct towards Ms Ferguson has, in my observation, been
different in tone from his conduct towards male colleagues of similar seniority. I do not wish to
overstate this - he can be curt with anyone - but the pattern is noticeable. I am aware other
members of the team hold similar views but they are uncomfortable speaking up. In candour, I
would be concerned about retaliation if this statement were shared in full with Mr Kellogg during
any disciplinary process, and I ask that my identity be managed carefully. I am also mindful that if
this statement were released under LGOIMA it should be withheld under s7(2)(a) as it contains my
personal information and that of junior staff who are not parties to the complaint.
Sign-off
